Title: Johannis Burchardi Argentinensis capellae pontificiae sacrorum rituum magistri Diarium, sive Rerum urbanarum commentarii (1483-1506). Texte latin publié intégralement pour la première fois d'après les manuscrits de Paris, de Rome et de Florence, avec introduction, notes, appendices, tables et index par L. Thuasne. Tome second (1492-1499)
Creator: Johann Burchard (d. 1506), papal master of ceremonies; edited by L. Thuasne
Publisher: Paris: Ernest Leroux, éditeur
Publication Date: 1884
Rights: Public Domain
Rights basis: the title page of this scan reads 'PARIS ERNEST LEROUX, ÉDITEUR' with the year read in the OCR as '4884'; the item record gives 1883 for the set and the Princeton shelfmark reads 'DG 797 .B9 1883 v.2'; the year is 1883 or 1884; the item record carries no rights field.
Language: lat (mixed: Latin diary with Thuasne's French introduction, notes and index)
Source: Internet Archive item johannisburchard02burc (archive.org/details/johannisburchard02burc), full-text file johannisburchard02burc_djvu.txt, fetched directly by the Library thread, October 2026.
Provenance note: Header prepended by the Library thread; the OCR text follows unchanged apart from this header. Nothing stripped, normalised, corrected, re-spaced or retyped. Latin and French sampled at opening, middle and end: readable, with scattered letter errors; the end is the French index. The cover pages are noise.
Content note: The second of Thuasne's three volumes of Burchard's diary: the papal master of ceremonies' record of the court of Rome from 1492 to 1499 (the election and reign of Alexander VI, the entry of Charles VIII, the consistories and processions). An insider record of the Renaissance papacy, day by day. Volumes 1 (1483-1492) and 3 (1500-1506) are not vendored.

et  punir  les  voleurs  et  les  bandits.  II  ne  fut  pas  donne  suite  a  ce  projet.  Voy.  Dea-eta 
consistorialia  ab  Alexandro  VI  usque  ad  Urbanum  VIII;  Bibl.  nat.,  mss.  12555,  fonds

menestriers  entre  lesdits  gentils-hommes  et  le  duc  de  Valentinois,  sonnans  toujours.

dees  de  cordons  d'or  et  de  perles ;

Qui  valoit  bien  trente  mille  ducats.
